scope: Catalogue-level operational census of manuscript procurement, production, shipment and paper/packing accounts centered on British Library Mss Eur Hodgson/12, 1824-1843.

source.catalogue: Cambridge Hodgson inventory, Mss Eur Hodgson/12
source.evidence_warning: Most records are catalogue-level. Exact figures, wording, currency notation and material correlations require folio-level verification.

cross_record_hypotheses: Hodgson's manuscript projects were managed through multiple commensuration systems: stanzas/slokas, leaves, prices, wages, paper units, bundles, packages, boxes and receipts.
Production and logistics were entered into the same reimbursement chain rather than treated as analytically separate operations.
Receipt counts changed scale across shipments: 109 bundles in 1827 versus nested boxes/packages/leaves/copies in 1829.
Mixed support in the 1827 bills creates a direct sheet-level test of whether paper stock correlates with date, actor, accounting stage or later assembly.
The 1843 bill potentially shows paper grade encoded economically, but the material basis of the two rates remains unknown until object inspection.
